cost.note: one chaotic iteration over the elaborated CFG with an interval per scalar slot: linear in nodes times slots per visit, a few visits per loop head under threshold widening, then at most six narrowing rounds; every corpus item settles in well under a second, the largest svcomp25-mini task (277 nodes) in about a second; the iteration budget is 500 node visits per wall second; revision 2 adds, only on a program carrying the translator's ite idiom and only after the plain pass has reached ERR, one case-split pass sharing the same budget of node visits, with at most eight splits open per partition (fewer when four sweeps of the program would not fit the budget left), and one verification of its hull: on hwmcc24-mini's translated machines the whole run stays within a second on all but the largest, which spend their budget in a few seconds as before

name: c-ai
notes: Interval abstract interpretation at C that certifies what it proves: the program is elaborated by c's own front end (embedded verbatim, so the node numbering and the slot names are the judge's), an interval per scalar slot is computed at every node by chaotic iteration — havoc reads are their whole type, every operation is evaluated in the interpreter's own types, branches refine by comparison against constants and other slots, through casts and constant offsets only where the conversion is the identity on the current interval, arrays are never tracked — with the program's own constants as widening thresholds at the back-edge targets and a narrowing whose every round is accepted only after the recomputed transformer is verified to stay below it; a post-fixpoint that excludes ERR is written as a {"schema": "ranges", "payload": {"kind": "range-invariant", ...}} certificate listing only the slots narrower than their type, discharged by c's `ranges` judge (revision 5) at the stop and never taken on faith here; at admission all five universal corpus items discharged. Sound for two's-complement wrap: a result that leaves its type takes the exact image of the wrap when that image is one interval and the whole type otherwise, never a guess — which is exactly what the `mutant_overclaims` control breaks, clamping instead, to write a certificate the judge refuses on overflow_1-2. Everything else is an honest partial: ERR reachable in the abstraction — which is what a false property, a relational invariant, a parity, or an array-content argument all look like to intervals; of svcomp25-mini's 42 universal tasks it proves four (nested_4, underapprox_2-2, while_infinite_loop_3, signextension-2), even.c stays partial on parity and overflow_1-2 stays partial as it must — a program outside the fragment, a spent iteration budget, and every exists question, since this search finds no witnesses. Never a bare claim. Budgets derive from the wall argument, never the clock. Revision 2 reads the branch-free ite the reverse edge btor2--c emits, `b ^ ((a ^ b) & -c)`, as the selection it is (case 1 yields a, case 0 yields b, an undetermined 1-bit c the hull of both; the generic reading whenever c is not within [0, 1] or an operand may be negative, where the identity of the conversions on the way is not argued), and adds a case-split pass that runs only when the plain iteration still reaches ERR on a program carrying the idiom: partitions of the interval state are streamed through each straight-line region, a split opening at an ite whose condition is undetermined, each case refined by the condition's own definition, an infeasible case dropped, the partitions hull-joined into every node's box and joined for good where a region ends; the hull is written as a certificate only when it is verified to be a post-fixpoint of the plain transformer, and otherwise the partial says that a disjunction is needed and names the first pc and slot where the box escapes. On the eight corpus programs of revision 1, which carry no idiom, every byte of output is the predecessor's. Corpus item 009 is the translator's output on a hand-written BTOR2 machine of two 8-bit registers behind muxes (r loads 200 or 100 or holds, q loads r or holds, both reset to 0, bad when either exceeds 200): the bounds are not a power of two less one, so revision 1's plain reading of the idiom's & and ^ reaches ERR while the selection reading writes a `ranges` certificate c's judge discharges. Corpus item 010 is the translator's output on hwmcc24-mini's safe4 (fib_37, three 19-bit registers), the measurement that fixes this revision's place: the case-split pass excludes ERR, and its hull is not inductive node by node — an ite-guarded increment `c ? s + 1 : s` computes s + 1 unconditionally into a temporary of its own, so the fact that the increment is taken only below the bound is a relation between the condition's slot and the operand's that one box per pc cannot state — and the honest partial names pc 20 and slot n28. That is the shape of every counter on the board: through this edge, with this certificate form, revision 2 settles none of hwmcc24-mini's 74 questions, and the reading it adds is worth exactly the machines whose registers are muxed among values already in range. The four controls are the three of revision 1 re-derived from this text and one aimed at the new fragment, the idiom read as its first case alone, which only item 009 can catch.
